exercises.q: It's no use trying to persuade her.
exercises.why: **Уговаривать** — угова́ривать (imperfective): to persuade, to talk (into), to urge. Wiktionary: уговори́ть + -ивать.

exercises.q: Match each word with its meaning (Wiktionary's definitions).
pairs: (intransitive) to speak, to talk, to converse (with)
exercises.why: From Wiktionary: говори́ть — to speak, to talk (perfective поговорить); проговори́ть — to say, to utter; заговори́ть — to begin to speak; разгова́ривать — (intransitive) to speak, to talk, to converse (with).
**уговорил** — уговори́ть (perfective): to persuade, to talk (into), to urge. Wiktionary: у- + говори́ть.

exercises.q: I don't like to be spoken to.
exercises.why: **заговаривают** — загова́ривать (imperfective): to begin to talk; to tire (someone) with one's talk, to talk someone's ear off; to exorcise, to cast a spell. Wiktionary: заговори́ть + -ивать.

exercises.q: It is difficult for the Japanese to articulate the sound of the r.
exercises.why: **выговаривать** — выгова́ривать (imperfective): to articulate, to pronounce, to utter; (colloquial) to tell off, to reprimand, to lecture; (colloquial) to reserve for oneself. Wiktionary: вы́говорить + -ивать.

exercises.why: **переговорю** — переговори́ть (perfective): to talk, to have a talk, to speak (to, with); (colloquial) to discuss, to cover; (colloquial) to talk down, to outtalk. Wiktionary: пере- + говори́ть.
